route.servesBothActions: confirm and override are two outcomes of one act: one eligibility rule, one concurrency guarantee, one audit path, one state-machine edge
route.throttleRationale: looser than the execution route's 10/60s because a settlement costs no provider legs and no deterministic analysis; a reviewer clearing a backlog should not be rate-limited as though each decision cost two hosted calls
route.crossTenantResponse: NotFound, indistinguishable from a non-existent resource

rejectedServerOwnedFields.mechanism: the DTO declares none of them and the global ValidationPipe is whitelist + forbidNonWhitelisted, so an undeclared property is a 400 before the controller runs
rejectedServerOwnedFields.reviewerIdentity: taken from the authenticated principal; not expressible in the body

eligibility.analysisFailedHasNoRow: a provider failure creates no analysis at all, so there is nothing to confirm
eligibility.clientSuppliedRefusedWith: 409 — a client-supplied snapshot carries no server-authored operational conclusion

confirmationSubject.what: the requiredBy entries that triggered the rule, each keyed by its refKind:ref pair
confirmationSubject.derivedFrom: the immutable persisted posture on resultSnapshot
confirmationSubject.derivedBy: the SAME confirmation rule version that produced the stored flag
confirmationSubject.ruleVersionMismatchBehaviour: REFUSE — re-deriving the subject under a newer rule would silently change the question the reviewer was originally asked, breaking §261's compute-once guarantee

overrideScope.addressableByTheAction: the classification of a named subject entry, and nothing else
overrideScope.changeThatChangesNothingIsRefused: recording it as a change would put a disagreement that did not happen into the audit trail
overrideScope.rationaleRequiredOnBothDecisions: including on a confirmation: a person putting their name to 'work may continue on this basis' with no stated reason is the record hardest to defend later

persistenceModel.reviewedConclusionCarries: both the Expert claim and the human value per entry, plus the posture, the contract version and the confirmation rule version

staleAnalysisBinding.mechanism: the reviewer names the analysis by id, and a superseded analysis is refused with a specific conflict
staleAnalysisBinding.confirmingASupersededAnalysis: 409 — a newer Expert analysis exists for this observation

guardImprovement263.what: the §263 evidence-integrity guard treated verification/current/ as frozen evidence
guardImprovement263.consequence: §264 failed the guard for keeping the current-state surface current
guardImprovement263.fix: verification/current/ is the LIVING index and is excluded from the frozen-evidence drift check; its updates are reported on their own line rather than hidden
guardImprovement263.guardStillNonVacuous: re-proven after the change — a deliberate mutation of the §262 report was caught by both mechanisms and PASS returned after restoration

testDefectsFoundInThisSection: the concurrency case originally raced two unrelated individual accounts; the loser was answered 404 because it had no access at all, so the case measured tenant isolation twice and concurrency not at all. It now races two members of one organization.
the reachability probe for that case sent an empty rationale and read 400 as proof of access — vacuous, because the validation pipe rejects before authorization. It now performs a real settlement.

six authentications from one address silently exceeded the 5-per-minute /auth/login throttle, leaving one reviewer with no token; the resulting 404 looked like a tenant refusal. Each auth call now uses its own address and the harness aborts on a missing token.
notDoneInThisSection: automatic finding reconciliation or report finalization
statedLimitations: NO CONSUMER READS effectiveDecision YET. §264 exposes the derivation and activates nothing, so the property that downstream features agree about authority is designed rather than demonstrated.

A SETTLED ANALYSIS CANNOT BE RE-OPENED. There is no un-confirm, no re-settle and no supersession of a human decision; the only path is a new Expert analysis, which starts its own settlement. Whether a reviewer may revise their own decision is a product question §264 did not decide.

CONFIRMING A SUPERSEDED ANALYSIS IS REFUSED OUTRIGHT. That is the fail-closed reading of 'do not accept a stale decision without detection'; a product that wanted to permit it with a warning would need a different answer.
GOVERNED CITATION REMAINS UNEXERCISED, unchanged from §262.
